first: Sequential Isolation Protocol for Reproducible LLM Inference Benchmarks. The Sequential Isolation Methodology cut average coefficient of variation from 15.2% to 2.2% for three open-source LLMs served with vLLM 0.9.1 on an A100. It brought 113 of 144 configurations below 3% CV, and its Infrastructure-as-Code and benchmark scripts are released for replication.
second: New Isolation Method Tames Run-to-Run Noise in LLM Inference Benchmarks. Researchers report a Sequential Isolation Protocol that lowered average coefficient of variation from 15.2% to 2.2% across three open-source LLMs served with vLLM 0.9.1 on an A100 GPU. The method brought 113 of 144 configurations under 3% CV, and its infrastructure-as-code and benchmark scripts have been released so others can replicate the results.

first: LLMs ported the TypeScript compiler to Rust, tsc-rs, as an early release. The author used LLMs to port the TypeScript compiler, checker and language server to Rust, releasing tsc-rs as an early build. OpenAI model attempts cost over $400,000 in API tokens and plateaued near 84% compatibility, while the release reports passing all 181,711 ported Go tests.
second: Early tsc-rs Release Ports TypeScript Compiler to Rust Using LLMs, Claims All 181,711 Go Tests Pass. An author has released tsc-rs as an early build, a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, checker, and language server created with LLM assistance. The project notes that OpenAI model attempts exceeded $400,000 in API token costs and stalled near 84% compatibility, while the release reports passing all 181,711 ported Go tests.

first: Claude Haiku 5.5 launches on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Haiku 5.5 is now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, with usage appearing on your AWS bill. Anthropic describes it as the fastest and most efficient model in the 5.5 family, costing around 75 percent less than Haiku 4.5 for most tasks.
second: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 Arrives on Amazon Bedrock, Billed Through AWS. Claude Haiku 5.5 is now accessible via Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, with charges appearing on customers' AWS bills. Anthropic positions it as the quickest and most efficient member of the 5.5 lineup, and says it costs roughly 75 percent less than Haiku 4.5 for most workloads.

first: AMU: lineage-gated memory blocks cross-department leakage in enterprise agents. The Analytical Memory Unit attaches a full lineage graph to each cached result and gates retrieval on permissions for every column touched. Against content-gated memory, which leaks 18.8-25.5% across departments, it keeps 81.5-82.6% of reuse with 13.8 microseconds worst-case overhead, and a proof of concept showed zero leaks over 9 round-trips.
second: New Memory Design Stops Enterprise AI Agents From Leaking Data Across Departments. Researchers propose the Analytical Memory Unit, which tags every cached result with its full lineage and checks permissions on each column it touches before reuse. Compared with content-gated memory, which leaked 18.8-25.5% across departments, the approach retained 81.5-82.6% of reuse with at most 13.8 microseconds of added overhead, and a proof of concept recorded zero leaks over nine round-trips.

first: Cornerstone cuts database diagnosis to 10 minutes with Strands Agents. Cornerstone OnDemand built its Orion AI multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock and the open source Strands Agents framework. Database diagnosis fell from 45 minutes to 10, a 78% reduction, and a three-person team delivered the system in six months.
second: Cornerstone OnDemand's Orion AI Slashes Database Diagnosis Time by 78%. Using Amazon Bedrock and the open source Strands Agents framework, Cornerstone OnDemand built its Orion multi-agent AI system, which cut database diagnosis from 45 minutes to 10. A three-person team delivered the system in six months.

first: Situation-conditioned thinking policy for long-running LLM agents. A lightweight learned policy predicts which thinking to activate and reaches 1.000 F1 on temporal-rule generalization. It raises DeepSeek reasoning F1 from 0.789 to 0.868 and cuts per-query processing from 0.3636 ms to 0.0382 ms at 30,000 situations.
second: New Lightweight Policy Chooses When LLM Agents Should Think, Boosting Accuracy and Slashing Processing Time. A learned policy that predicts which kind of thinking a long-running LLM agent should activate reached perfect 1.000 F1 on temporal-rule generalization. It lifted DeepSeek reasoning F1 from 0.789 to 0.868, while cutting per-query processing from 0.3636 ms to 0.0382 ms across 30,000 situations.

first: Automated judge errors misrepresent the most informative uncertainty quantifiers. A meta-analysis finds automated judges are the norm for evaluating uncertainty quantifiers, and experiments compare them with human judgements across 4 LLMs and 7 UQs. A judge's performance only coarsely predicts how its errors affect evaluation, and judgement errors most misrepresent the most informative UQs.
second: Automated Judges Can Distort Rankings of the Most Useful Uncertainty Quantifiers. A meta-analysis shows that automated judges are now the standard way to evaluate uncertainty quantifiers, so experiments comparing them with human judgments across 4 LLMs and 7 UQs were conducted. The results show that a judge's overall performance only loosely predicts how its errors will skew evaluations, and that these errors most distort the assessment of the most informative UQs.

first: RunningTab: environment-side task ledger keeps LLM agents from missing requirements. RunningTab keeps a per-task record in the environment, logging each file read with provenance and each listed but unopened file as a candidate. A finish check surfaces open requirements before the agent can stop, and the approach beat plain direct workspace interaction on three benchmarks with three LLMs, usually keeping the values a deliverable needs once seen.
second: New RunningTab Ledger Helps AI Agents Stop Overlooking Task Requirements. RunningTab, an environment-side task ledger, logs each file an LLM agent reads along with its source and flags listed but unopened files as candidates, then runs a finish check that surfaces open requirements before the agent can stop. Across three benchmarks and three LLMs, it outperformed plain direct workspace interaction and generally retained values a deliverable needs once they were seen.

first: langchain-core 1.6.7 fixes Bedrock Converse redacted content output. langchain-core 1.6.7 includes OpenAI redacted_content in v1 output for Bedrock Converse. It also adds Python 3.14 hardening around inspect.signature.
second: langchain-core 1.6.7 Adds Redacted Content Handling for Bedrock Converse and Python 3.14 Hardening. The latest langchain-core release, version 1.6.7, corrects how Bedrock Converse redacted content is output and includes OpenAI redacted_content in v1 output for that service. It also introduces hardening for Python 3.14 around inspect.signature.

first: Microsoft releases Agent Lightning v1.0 for RL training with real agent harnesses. Agent Lightning v1.0 is an RL framework of about 3,500 lines that trains the same agent harness used in deployment, using an LLM proxy. On SWE-bench Verified, a coding pipeline lifted Qwen3.5-9B Pass@1 from 41.8% to 56.4% using about 6,000 samples, and it runs as Kubernetes jobs.
second: Microsoft's Agent Lightning v1.0 Lets Teams Reinforcement-Train AI Agents Inside the Harnesses They Actually Ship With. Microsoft has launched Agent Lightning v1.0, a compact roughly 3,500-line reinforcement learning framework that trains the same agent harness used in production via an LLM proxy. In a SWE-bench Verified test, a coding pipeline raised Qwen3.5-9B's Pass@1 score from 41.8% to 56.4% using about 6,000 samples, and the system runs as Kubernetes jobs.

first: EngramEdit: decoupled factual edits in DeepSeek Engram-style memory. EngramEdit updates shared n-gram embeddings in conditional memory, penalizing frequently reused ones more strongly, which largely preserves unrelated knowledge. It reaches near-perfect editing success, and under chain-of-thought prompting its multi-hop accuracy is nearly three times the strongest baseline's.
second: New Method Lets Researchers Surgically Correct Facts in DeepSeek Engram-Style Memory Without Collateral Damage. EngramEdit, a technique for revising facts stored in DeepSeek Engram-style conditional memory, adjusts shared n-gram embeddings and applies stronger penalties to frequently reused ones, which largely keeps unrelated knowledge intact. It achieves near-perfect editing success, and with chain-of-thought prompting its multi-hop accuracy is almost three times that of the best baseline.

first: SkillForge: Lifecycle-Managed Skill Libraries for RL-Trained LLM Agents. SkillForge manages an agent's skill library through fitness-driven trial, active, stable and retired states, and reports the highest aggregate success rate across several interactive benchmarks. It improves on the strongest baseline by up to 7.8% relative and releases SkillFurnace, a dataset of over 5,000 annotated records.
second: SkillForge Tops Interactive Benchmarks With Lifecycle-Managed Skill Libraries for LLM Agents. Researchers introduced SkillForge, a system that moves an RL-trained LLM agent's skills through trial, active, stable, and retired stages based on fitness, and it posts the best aggregate success rate across several interactive benchmarks, beating the strongest baseline by up to 7.8% relative. The team also released SkillFurnace, a dataset of more than 5,000 annotated records.

first: LittleBit-2 compresses LLMs below one bit per weight via factorization. LittleBit factorizes each dense weight matrix into binarized low-rank latent factors restored by learned scales, targeting 1.0 to 0.1 bits per weight. LittleBit-2 adds an opt-in Joint-ITQ initialization with no extra inference overhead, and the README advises pinning transformers 4.51.x to reproduce the paper results.
second: LittleBit-2 Pushes LLM Compression Below One Bit per Weight Using Factorization. LittleBit-2 is a new method that shrinks large language models to under one bit per weight by splitting each dense weight matrix into binarized low-rank factors rescaled by learned scales, aiming for anywhere from 1.0 down to 0.1 bits per weight. An optional Joint-ITQ initialization adds no inference overhead, and the project's README recommends pinning transformers to version 4.51.x to match the paper's results.

first: Automated persuasion evaluation methods agree only weakly across models. Nine adapted automated persuasion methods were run on the same fifteen LLMs, with a mean Spearman rho of 0.25. Refusing some tasks but not others lowers agreement between the methods by about a quarter.
second: Tools for Measuring AI Persuasiveness Disagree on Which Models Rank Highest. Nine automated persuasion benchmarks, each adapted from prior work, were applied to the same fifteen large language models, yielding only weak agreement in model rankings (mean Spearman rho of 0.25). Models that refuse some persuasion tasks but not others further reduce cross-method agreement by roughly a quarter.

first: InsClaimBench: LLM reliability drops along insurance claim decision chains. InsClaimBench evaluates six LLMs on 3,780 insurance claim cases across auto, property and health lines. Payout decisions reach 74.23-80.19% accuracy, but joint decision and amount accuracy falls to 47.54-73.15%, while atomic-rule accuracy of 95.48% yields at most 36.90% exact match on full rule vectors.
second: Insurance Claim AI Stumbles Once Decisions Chain Together, Benchmark Finds. A new benchmark testing six LLMs on 3,780 auto, property and health insurance claims shows that while individual payout decisions are right 74-80% of the time, accuracy drops to 47-73% when decisions and amounts must be correct together. Models handle single rules well at 95.48%, yet match full rule sets exactly in at most 36.90% of cases.

first: PhysEvo: a meta-agent evolves tools and skills around a frozen robot model. A meta-agent revises a frozen model's tools and skills from failure diagnoses, with no weight updates or separately trained action policy. It reaches 62.00% success on 42 RoboDojo tasks against 47.17% for the one-shot Astra agent, and 84.00% on five real-world tasks across 25 trials.
second: Meta-Agent Rewrites Robot Tools and Skills Without Touching Model Weights, Beating Astra on Simulated Tasks. PhysEvo, a system that refines a frozen robot model's tools and skills based on diagnoses of its failures, achieved 62.00% success on 42 RoboDojo tasks versus 47.17% for the one-shot Astra agent, and reached 84.00% across 25 trials on five real-world tasks. It requires no weight updates or separately trained action policy.

first: AWS guide builds context-aware OpenClaw assistant on AgentCore runtime. The assistant sends text chats to Claude Haiku 4.5 and image turns to Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Bedrock. It runs on AgentCore runtime, which bills only for active compute and requires port 8080 with GET /ping and POST /invocations, and the whole stack deploys from one CloudFormation template.
second: New AWS Guide Shows How to Deploy a Context-Aware OpenClaw Assistant on AgentCore. An AWS guide walks developers through building a context-aware OpenClaw assistant that routes text chats to Claude Haiku 4.5 and image turns to Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Bedrock. The assistant runs on AgentCore runtime, which charges only for active compute and expects port 8080 with GET /ping and POST /invocations, and the full stack deploys from a single CloudFormation template.

first: openai 3.26.1 corrects custom voice creation parameters. openai 3.26.1 fixes the parameters used to create custom voices.
second: New OpenAI 3.26.1 Release Repairs Settings Used to Build Custom Voices. Version 3.26.1 from OpenAI addresses errors in the parameters that govern custom voice creation. The update corrects those settings so users can generate custom voices as intended.

first: Qlik Answers runs on Amazon Bedrock with routing, retrieval and guardrails. Qlik Answers, generally available since February 2026, serves more than 40,000 customers. Its model layer calls Amazon Bedrock for chat, embeddings and reranking, with Bedrock Guardrails and a grounding check on every answer, and document retrieval on Amazon OpenSearch Service.
second: Qlik Answers Built on Amazon Bedrock, Using Guardrails and OpenSearch Retrieval for 40,000+ Customers. Qlik Answers, generally available since February 2026 and serving more than 40,000 customers, routes its model calls for chat, embeddings and reranking through Amazon Bedrock. Each answer passes a Bedrock Guardrails check and a grounding check, while document retrieval runs on Amazon OpenSearch Service.

first: Query-side distractors break retrieval instructions in embedding models. Embedding models can fail to follow simple retrieval instructions when query-side distractors are present. Fine-tuning with added query-side distractors gives substantial improvements with minimal effect on other tasks.
second: Adding Distractors to Training Queries Fixes Embedding Models' Trouble Following Retrieval Instructions. Researchers found that embedding models often struggle to obey straightforward retrieval instructions when distracting content appears in the query. Fine-tuning the models with such query-side distractors added to training data produced large gains while barely affecting performance on other tasks.

first: fastmcp 4.1.0 adds security fixes with several breaking input changes. FastMCP 4.1.0 is a maintenance release with fixes across OpenAPI, proxies, auth, tasks and the CLI, plus full Python 3.15 support, and it tightens some inputs it previously accepted. Existing MultiAuth sessions and tasks move to new ownership scopes, and HTTP sessions now expire after 30 minutes of idle time.
second: FastMCP 4.1.0 Ships Security Patches, Stricter Input Validation, and Python 3.15 Support. The FastMCP 4.1.0 maintenance release patches issues across OpenAPI, proxies, authentication, tasks, and the CLI, and adds full Python 3.15 compatibility. Developers should note that it now rejects some inputs it previously accepted, existing MultiAuth sessions and tasks move to new ownership scopes, and HTTP sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity.

first: Multi-Agent LLM Workflow with MCP Solver Docs Boosts Scheduling Models. Multi-agent LLM workflows with a Model Context Protocol server for solver documentation raised runnable constraint programming scripts from 14.8% to 59.3% across six scheduling problems. The workflow reached 80.6% on the four less complex problems, while tightly coupled intralogistics models remain an open challenge.
second: LLM Agents Paired With Solver Documentation Lift Scheduling Code From 14.8% to 59.3% Success. A multi-agent LLM pipeline that consults a Model Context Protocol server holding solver docs produced runnable constraint programming scripts for six scheduling problems, rising from 14.8% to 59.3%. It hit 80.6% on the four simpler problems, but tightly coupled intralogistics models still stump the system.

first: Atlassian and OpenAI expand partnership to connect models with enterprise knowledge. Atlassian and OpenAI are expanding their partnership, according to the announcement. The expansion aims to connect frontier models with enterprise knowledge so teams can plan, build, and deliver work.
second: OpenAI Deepens Tie-Up With Atlassian to Bring Frontier AI Into Company Workflows. Atlassian and OpenAI have widened their partnership, with the goal of linking advanced models to internal enterprise data so workplace teams can map out, create, and ship projects more effectively.

first: langchain 1.4.4 retries summarization on context overflow, raises FastMCP floor. langchain 1.4.4 makes SummarizationMiddleware retry its summary step when context overflows. The package's minimum FastMCP requirement is now 4.0.11.
second: LangChain 1.4.4 Adds Summary Retries for Context Overflow and Bumps Minimum FastMCP to 4.0.11. The new LangChain 1.4.4 release has SummarizationMiddleware retry its summary step when context overflows. It also raises the package's minimum FastMCP requirement to version 4.0.11.

first: SWE-Game: benchmark of 247 tasks for coding agents building Godot games. SWE-Game gives coding agents 247 tasks built on 41 executable Godot reference games, and the best overall scores stay below 60 out of 100 on construction tasks. Executable checks judged agent-built games better than a video-based VLM judge, 92.59% versus 78.41% balanced accuracy, while rubric visual scores correlate 0.829 with human ratings.
second: New Godot Benchmark Finds Coding Agents Still Fall Short of 60/100 on Game Construction. SWE-Game, a 247-task benchmark built on 41 executable Godot reference games, shows top agents scoring under 60 out of 100 on construction tasks. Executable checks outperformed a video-based VLM judge in identifying agent-built games (92.59% vs. 78.41% balanced accuracy), and rubric visual scores correlated 0.829 with human ratings.

first: LiveMACEBench: Process-Aware Live-Market Benchmark for LLM Agents. LiveMACEBench evaluates five frontier LLMs on live financial markets under tool use, persistent memory, rule following and multi-agent collaboration. Over 30 days, realized returns often diverged from capability-specific measures, and similar outcomes came from markedly different mechanism use.
second: Winning Trades Can Hide Flawed Reasoning, New Live-Market Test for AI Agents Finds. A 30-day live financial market benchmark, LiveMACEBench, tested five leading LLMs on tool use, memory, rule compliance and multi-agent teamwork. The study found profits frequently failed to track these individual capability scores, and agents with similar results often relied on very different underlying processes.

first: Amazon Quick and Bedrock Knowledge Bases add real-time ACL checks for RAG. Amazon Quick and Bedrock Knowledge Bases check document permissions against the source at query time, on top of filtering by stored ACLs. Candidate documents are verified against Google Drive APIs, and unauthorized documents are dropped before the LLM sees them.
second: Amazon Quick and Bedrock Knowledge Bases Now Verify Document Permissions at Query Time. Amazon has added live access-control checks to Amazon Quick and Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which confirm document permissions against the source system when a query runs, in addition to filtering by stored ACLs. Candidate documents are checked against Google Drive APIs, and any document a user isn't authorized to see is removed before the LLM receives it.

first: AWS Lambda durable functions turn DevOps Agent findings into approved remediations. EventBridge passes DevOps Agent's investigation events to a Lambda durable function, which asks Amazon Bedrock to propose fixes. Bedrock can choose only from an allowlist of approved Lambda tools, read-only tools run automatically, and changes pause for human approval without consuming compute.
second: Human Sign-Off Gates AI-Proposed Fixes in New AWS Lambda Remediation Workflow. AWS is pairing DevOps Agent investigations with Lambda durable functions so that EventBridge routes findings to a function that asks Amazon Bedrock for fix proposals. Bedrock is limited to an allowlist of approved Lambda tools, read-only actions run automatically, and any change waits for human approval without consuming compute while paused.

first: Inherit-MAS: multi-agent workflow inheritance cuts worker tokens. With GPT-4o-mini workers, Inherit-MAS scores 55.4% completion on WorkBench and 49.7% joint F1 on HotpotQA FullWiki. Compared with rerunning the same controller with execution inheritance disabled, it cuts worker-token usage by 29.1% and 34.6% on the two benchmarks.
second: Inherit-MAS Trims Worker Token Use by About a Third Across Two Benchmarks. Using GPT-4o-mini workers, the Inherit-MAS multi-agent workflow system reached 55.4% completion on WorkBench and 49.7% joint F1 on HotpotQA FullWiki. Relative to rerunning the same controller with execution inheritance turned off, it reduced worker-token consumption by 29.1% on WorkBench and 34.6% on HotpotQA.

first: AutoResearch at Production Scale: Five Failure Modes and a Multi-Agent Fix. Over twelve weeks and 220+ experiments on two representation-learning systems for a book recommendation pipeline, the authors observed five recurring failure modes, including agent memory decay. Their scaffolding gave a 1.82x Recall@6 lift and 2.1x coherence lift over hand-tuned baselines, and the agent's text-only fallback expanded catalog coverage 5.8x.
second: Study Maps Five Ways Automated AI Research Breaks Down at Scale, Then Shows a Multi-Agent Workaround. Over twelve weeks and more than 220 experiments on two representation-learning systems for a book recommender, researchers identified five recurring failure modes, including agent memory decay. Their multi-agent scaffolding delivered a 1.82x lift in Recall@6 and a 2.1x coherence lift over hand-tuned baselines, while a text-only fallback widened catalog coverage 5.8x.

first: UniSkill: actor-aligned skill proposals reach 98.4% on ALFWorld. UniSkill, which proposes skillbank edits from trajectories, reaches 98.4% success on ALFWorld and 84.7% on WebShop. It stays effective on ALFWorld with a smaller policy backbone, and its implementation is public on GitHub.
second: New UniSkill Method Hits 98.4% on ALFWorld, Also Scores 84.7% on WebShop. Researchers have introduced UniSkill, a system that suggests edits to a skillbank based on agent trajectories, achieving 98.4% success on ALFWorld and 84.7% on WebShop. The method remains effective on ALFWorld when paired with a smaller policy backbone, and its code is publicly available on GitHub.

first: langsmith 0.14.5 adds address types and LANGSMITH_REVISION_ID support. langsmith 0.14.5 adds AgentAddress, ExperimentAddress and EvaluatorAddress types, and reads LANGSMITH_REVISION_ID into run revision_id. It also fixes redaction of license key and API key salt assignments.
second: LangSmith 0.14.5 Brings New Address Classes and Revision Tracking, Plus a Redaction Fix. The latest LangSmith release introduces AgentAddress, ExperimentAddress and EvaluatorAddress types, and now picks up LANGSMITH_REVISION_ID to populate a run's revision_id. Version 0.14.5 also patches redaction of license key and API key salt assignments.

first: RoboQuest: Benchmark for Physical Agents That Search and Test. RoboQuest is a benchmark of ten mobile manipulation tasks centered on search, manipulation-based inspection and interactive testing. The best of five frontier agents succeeds in only 23% of episodes, a policy fine-tuned on the released demonstrations almost never succeeds, and agents often stop exploring too early.
second: New RoboQuest Benchmark Exposes Limits of Physical AI Agents at Search-and-Test Tasks. Researchers released RoboQuest, a ten-task mobile manipulation benchmark focused on searching, inspecting objects by handling them, and interactively testing. Even the top of five leading agents succeeds in just 23% of episodes, a policy fine-tuned on the released demonstrations almost never succeeds, and agents frequently give up exploring too soon.

first: MIMESIS: Learned User Simulator for Training Interactive Agents. MIMESIS is a 9B user simulator trained on human conversations that reaches a SOUL-Index of 65.7, above the strongest frontier model. Agents trained against the frozen simulator outperform agents trained with GPT-5.5 under all nine unseen user simulators, and MIMESIS improves behavioral fidelity by 13.4 points over Claude-Opus-5.
second: MIMESIS, a 9B Open User Simulator, Beats Frontier Models at Mimicking Human Users and Training Stronger Agents. Trained on human conversations, the 9B MIMESIS simulator scores 65.7 on the SOUL-Index, ahead of the strongest frontier model, and improves behavioral fidelity by 13.4 points over Claude-Opus-5. Agents trained against the frozen simulator outperform those trained with GPT-5.5 across all nine unseen user simulators.

first: RobotWorld: 84-Task Benchmark for Multimodal Robot-Use Agents. RobotWorld is a simulated benchmark of 84 robot-use tasks with explicit interaction budgets and executable success checks. Agents can build sophisticated perception and control workflows but often fail to turn them into completed tasks, and which model succeeds more depends on task type.
second: New Simulator Tests Whether Robot AI Agents Can Actually Finish Jobs. Researchers have released RobotWorld, a simulated benchmark with 84 robot-use tasks, each with a fixed interaction budget and automated success checks. The study finds agents often build capable perception and control pipelines yet fail to complete the tasks, and that the better-performing model varies with the type of task.

first: langchain-core 1.6.9 lets with_retry accept a callable argument. langchain-core 1.6.9 changes with_retry so it accepts a callable.
second: langchain-core 1.6.9 Lets with_retry Take a Callable Argument. The latest langchain-core release, version 1.6.9, updates with_retry so that it can now accept a callable as an argument.

first: System Switch: when a fast decision model should defer to reasoning. Among their errors, small decision models choose item collection 1.6-1.8 times more often than chance, and deferring their least confident 30% of decisions to a reasoning model beats random deferral by +0.13 under the original option order. In closed-loop Doom over 33 games no variant reached the exit, though code, prompts, data and logs are released.
second: Study Finds Small AI Decision Models Overpick Item Collection; Deferring Uncertain Choices to a Reasoning Model Helps. Small decision models choose item collection 1.6 to 1.8 times more often than chance, according to the research. Routing their least confident 30% of decisions to a reasoning model outperforms random deferral by 0.13 under the original option order, though no variant reached the exit in closed-loop Doom across 33 games; code, prompts, data and logs are released.

first: Agent plasticity: a metric for how agents improve from experience. Agent plasticity measures how efficiently an agent turns experience into held-out gains, and frontier models differ sharply in their improvement trajectories. Gains often transfer only partially to out-of-distribution conditions, and the top endpoint agent is not always the most efficient learner.
second: New 'Agent Plasticity' Metric Gauges How Well AI Agents Learn From Experience. Researchers have proposed agent plasticity, a measure of how efficiently an AI agent converts experience into gains on held-out tasks, and find that frontier models vary widely in their improvement trajectories. The gains often apply only partially to out-of-distribution conditions, and the agent that performs best at the end is not necessarily the most efficient learner.

first: Sequential Isolation Protocol for Reproducible LLM Inference Benchmarks. The Sequential Isolation Methodology cut average coefficient of variation from 15.2% to 2.2% for three open-source LLMs served with vLLM 0.9.1 on an A100. It brought 113 of 144 configurations below 3% CV, and its Infrastructure-as-Code and benchmark scripts are released for replication.
second: New Isolation Method Tightens LLM Benchmark Variability From 15% to 2%. Researchers introduced a Sequential Isolation Protocol that lowered average coefficient of variation from 15.2% to 2.2% when benchmarking three open-source LLMs served with vLLM 0.9.1 on an A100 GPU. Of 144 configurations, 113 fell below 3% variation, and the team has released its Infrastructure-as-Code and benchmark scripts so others can replicate the results.

first: LLMs ported the TypeScript compiler to Rust, tsc-rs, as an early release. The author used LLMs to port the TypeScript compiler, checker and language server to Rust, releasing tsc-rs as an early build. OpenAI model attempts cost over $400,000 in API tokens and plateaued near 84% compatibility, while the release reports passing all 181,711 ported Go tests.
second: Early Rust Port of TypeScript Compiler Built With LLMs Claims Full Pass on 181,711 Tests. An author has released tsc-rs, an early build of a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, checker, and language server created with LLM assistance. The project's OpenAI model attempts reportedly consumed over $400,000 in API tokens and stalled near 84% compatibility, while the release says all 181,711 ported Go tests pass.

first: Claude Haiku 5.5 launches on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Haiku 5.5 is now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, with usage appearing on your AWS bill. Anthropic describes it as the fastest and most efficient model in the 5.5 family, costing around 75 percent less than Haiku 4.5 for most tasks.
second: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 Hits Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, Billed Through Your AWS Account. Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 is now live on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, with usage showing up on customers' AWS bills. Anthropic calls it the fastest and most efficient model in the 5.5 lineup, and says it costs roughly 75 percent less than Haiku 4.5 for most tasks.

Compared with content-gated memory, which leaked 18.8-25.5% of data across departments, the approach retained 81.5-82.6% of reuse with at most 13.8 microseconds of added overhead, and a proof of concept recorded zero leaks across 9 round-trips.

first: Cornerstone cuts database diagnosis to 10 minutes with Strands Agents. Cornerstone OnDemand built its Orion AI multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock and the open source Strands Agents framework. Database diagnosis fell from 45 minutes to 10, a 78% reduction, and a three-person team delivered the system in six months.
second: Cornerstone OnDemand's Orion AI Slashes Database Diagnosis Time by 78%. Using Amazon Bedrock and the open source Strands Agents framework, Cornerstone OnDemand built its multi-agent Orion AI system, which shortened database diagnosis from 45 minutes to 10. A three-person team completed the build in six months.

It raises DeepSeek reasoning F1 from 0.789 to 0.868 and cuts per-query processing from 0.3636 ms to 0.0382 ms at 30,000 situations.
second: Lightweight Policy Picks When Long-Running AI Agents Should Think Harder. second: Automated Judges Can Distort Rankings of the Most Useful Uncertainty Quantifiers. A meta-analysis shows that automated judges are now the standard way to assess uncertainty quantifiers, so experiments comparing them with human judgments across 4 LLMs and 7 UQ methods were run. The study finds that a judge's overall accuracy is only a rough guide to how its errors will skew evaluations, and that these errors most often misrepresent the most informative uncertainty quantifiers.

first: RunningTab: environment-side task ledger keeps LLM agents from missing requirements. RunningTab keeps a per-task record in the environment, logging each file read with provenance and each listed but unopened file as a candidate. A finish check surfaces open requirements before the agent can stop, and the approach beat plain direct workspace interaction on three benchmarks with three LLMs, usually keeping the values a deliverable needs once seen.
second: New RunningTab Ledger Stops AI Agents From Overlooking Task Requirements. RunningTab, an environment-side task ledger, records each file an LLM agent reads along with its source and flags listed but unopened files as candidates, then runs a finish check that surfaces open requirements before the agent can stop. Across three benchmarks and three LLMs, the approach outperformed plain direct workspace interaction and generally retained the values a deliverable needs once they were encountered.

first: langchain-core 1.6.7 fixes Bedrock Converse redacted content output. langchain-core 1.6.7 includes OpenAI redacted_content in v1 output for Bedrock Converse. It also adds Python 3.14 hardening around inspect.signature.
second: langchain-core 1.6.7 Adds Python 3.14 Hardening and Bedrock Converse Fixes. The latest langchain-core release, version 1.6.7, corrects how Bedrock Converse handles redacted content, carrying OpenAI redacted_content into v1 output. It also strengthens compatibility with Python 3.14 around inspect.signature.

first: Microsoft releases Agent Lightning v1.0 for RL training with real agent harnesses. Agent Lightning v1.0 is an RL framework of about 3,500 lines that trains the same agent harness used in deployment, using an LLM proxy. On SWE-bench Verified, a coding pipeline lifted Qwen3.5-9B Pass@1 from 41.8% to 56.4% using about 6,000 samples, and it runs as Kubernetes jobs.
second: Microsoft's Agent Lightning 1.0 Trains AI Agents Inside Their Live Deployment Harness. Microsoft has launched Agent Lightning v1.0, a roughly 3,500-line reinforcement learning framework that trains agents using the same harness they run in production, routed through an LLM proxy. In a SWE-bench Verified test, a coding pipeline raised Qwen3.5-9B's Pass@1 score from 41.8% to 56.4% using about 6,000 samples, and the framework runs as Kubernetes jobs.

first: EngramEdit: decoupled factual edits in DeepSeek Engram-style memory. EngramEdit updates shared n-gram embeddings in conditional memory, penalizing frequently reused ones more strongly, which largely preserves unrelated knowledge. It reaches near-perfect editing success, and under chain-of-thought prompting its multi-hop accuracy is nearly three times the strongest baseline's.
second: New EngramEdit Method Fixes Facts in DeepSeek-Style Memory Without Disturbing Unrelated Knowledge. Researchers introduced EngramEdit, a technique for correcting specific facts in Engram-style conditional memory by adjusting shared n-gram embeddings and applying heavier penalties to frequently reused ones, which largely keeps unrelated knowledge intact. The method achieves near-perfect editing success, and with chain-of-thought prompting its multi-hop accuracy is nearly three times that of the strongest baseline.

first: SkillForge: Lifecycle-Managed Skill Libraries for RL-Trained LLM Agents. SkillForge manages an agent's skill library through fitness-driven trial, active, stable and retired states, and reports the highest aggregate success rate across several interactive benchmarks. It improves on the strongest baseline by up to 7.8% relative and releases SkillFurnace, a dataset of over 5,000 annotated records.
second: SkillForge Tracks Agent Skills Through Trial, Active, Stable and Retired Stages, Lifting Benchmark Success Up to 7.8%. Researchers introduced SkillForge, a system that governs an RL-trained LLM agent's skill library using fitness scores to move skills between trial, active, stable and retired states, and it posted the top aggregate success rate across several interactive benchmarks. The work also releases SkillFurnace, a dataset of more than 5,000 annotated records.

first: RobotWorld: 84-Task Benchmark for Multimodal Robot-Use Agents. RobotWorld is a simulated benchmark of 84 robot-use tasks with explicit interaction budgets and executable success checks. Agents can build sophisticated perception and control workflows but often fail to turn them into completed tasks, and which model succeeds more depends on task type.
second: RoboQuest: Benchmark for Physical Agents That Search and Test. RoboQuest is a benchmark of ten mobile manipulation tasks centered on search, manipulation-based inspection and interactive testing. The best of five frontier agents succeeds in only 23% of episodes, a policy fine-tuned on the released demonstrations almost never succeeds, and agents often stop exploring too early.

first: Claude Haiku 5.5 launches on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Haiku 5.5 is now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS, with usage appearing on your AWS bill. Anthropic describes it as the fastest and most efficient model in the 5.5 family, costing around 75 percent less than Haiku 4.5 for most tasks.
second: AWS guide builds context-aware OpenClaw assistant on AgentCore runtime. The assistant sends text chats to Claude Haiku 4.5 and image turns to Claude Sonnet 4.5 on Bedrock. It runs on AgentCore runtime, which bills only for active compute and requires port 8080 with GET /ping and POST /invocations, and the whole stack deploys from one CloudFormation template.

second: SWE-Game: benchmark of 247 tasks for coding agents building Godot games. SWE-Game gives coding agents 247 tasks built on 41 executable Godot reference games, and the best overall scores stay below 60 out of 100 on construction tasks. Executable checks judged agent-built games better than a video-based VLM judge, 92.59% versus 78.41% balanced accuracy, while rubric visual scores correlate 0.829 with human ratings.

first: LiveMACEBench: Process-Aware Live-Market Benchmark for LLM Agents. LiveMACEBench evaluates five frontier LLMs on live financial markets under tool use, persistent memory, rule following and multi-agent collaboration. Over 30 days, realized returns often diverged from capability-specific measures, and similar outcomes came from markedly different mechanism use.
second: Multi-Agent LLM Workflow with MCP Solver Docs Boosts Scheduling Models. Multi-agent LLM workflows with a Model Context Protocol server for solver documentation raised runnable constraint programming scripts from 14.8% to 59.3% across six scheduling problems. The workflow reached 80.6% on the four less complex problems, while tightly coupled intralogistics models remain an open challenge.
